answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network requires new identities at the dawn of registration to solve memory-hard cryptographic puzzles, logging completion proofs in a decentralized vault before joining the consensus mesa. This forces adversaries to dedicate physical high-bandwidth memory capacity and bus throughput per fake agent, preventing cheap virtualization. However, it penalizes lightweight edge agents with scarce RAM and cannot stop adversaries wielding enterprise memory clusters.
